prompts.prompt: Create ONE landscape 3:2 Wonder Together Curiosity scenic explainer plate for a Grade 2 family. Question it serves: "What is waking up inside this little bean?" The picture is a complete single coherent scene, NOT a poster, worksheet, panel grid or title card. Luxury that cares: painterly botanical gouache and fine hand-drawn ink on warm ivory cotton paper, tactile subtle grain, beautifully composed quiet morning light, muted sage, warm grey and earth brown. Concept dominates: a warm wooden windowsill with one small pale ceramic planter holding dark moist soil, shown in an integrated magnified cutaway across the front of the pot. A large anatomically plausible bean below the soil surface has a reddish-tan split seed coat, two plump pale cotyledons (stored food), a tiny curved cream root just emerging DOWN, and tiny embryonic shoot between the halves. It is an educational magnification, not a huge bean literally sitting atop the pot. The soil has visible pockets of air and a few water droplets. Use ONLY three modest burnt-orange handwritten field-note labels in the scene, with delicate clear leader lines: "water in" pointing toward the bean, "stored food" pointing to a cotyledon, "first root" pointing to the emerging root. No long explanation and no title or footer inside art. The planter and cutaway take most of the image. A softly washed window, pale linen curtain, distant garden and morning shadows make this a full scene, spacious but not empty. Include Wonder Together recurring pair, Big Wonderer and Little Wonderer, small at the left edge sharing attention toward the bean: gender-neutral nonhuman minimal Pebble Guides, rounded warm-grey/tan capsule silhouettes, tiny integrated ear nubs, tiny dot eyes, subtle nose dash, short mitten-like arms. Big is 1.5 times Little's height, beside and slightly behind; Little gently points. They are quiet diagram actors, not literal bears or teddy toys; no fur, clothes, tails, paws, plush seams, snouts, human hair, or mascot expressions. Reserve strongest orange only for mechanism cues, keep whole scene softly filled, tender and sophisticated. No clipart, neon, photorealism, decorative sparkles, brand logo or typography-heavy layout. Make the scientific mechanism unmistakable at phone size.

An ILLUSTRATION, not a photograph: one 3:2 landscape Wonder Together Curiosity explainer painted as a spare hand-drawn children's natural-history field guide. Flat gouache washes, visible pencil and ink outlines, large areas of unpainted cream paper, intentionally simplified forms, NO photographic textures, NO 3D rendering, NO realistic objects. Quiet luxury and tenderness. Question (not printed): "What is waking up inside this little bean?" One coherent windowsill scene. The central large pale clay pot has an illustrated cutaway exposing dark soil and ONE enlarged bean seed below the surface: reddish seed coat split, two pale stored-food halves, tiny shoot tucked between the halves, ONE short curved root protrudes down. NOTHING leafy growing above the soil yet. Two orange hand-drawn annotations "stored food" and "first root", with thin leader lines to their parts. A tiny blue water droplet beside the seed suggests dampness. Broad muted sage window frame, soft sketched garden beyond, warm light drawn with pale drybrush. The mechanism must be very clear, and the image calm, spacious, sophisticated. On the left, small Wonder Together Pebble Guides quietly share gaze toward the seed. Big Wonderer 1.5x Little's height, beside and slightly behind. Simple flat warm-grey rounded capsule silhouettes, almost no limbs, two tiny ink dot eyes, a tiny nose dash, tiny integrated ear nubs. No fingers, fur, clothes, snouts, paws, tails, toy seams, 3D volume, or mascot poses. Pair should look like flat ink diagram actors. Scene fills the landscape, yet paper breathes around contours. ONLY those two handwritten orange labels, no other words, no book titles, no header, no footer. Absolutely no photorealistic lighting, stock imagery, toys, cute clipart, panels, grids, posters, logos or neon.

Generate ONE NEW companion 3:2 landscape single-scene Wonder Together Curiosity illustration. Attached image is STYLE AND CHARACTER REFERENCE only. Retain its flat hand-drawn gouache and pencil, cream paper, sage window, clay pot, minimal flat warm-grey Pebble Guides (Big beside and behind Little, 1.5x height). No photorealism or 3D. New question served (not printed): "How does a root find its way when it cannot see?" A slightly wider windowsill scene with the pale clay planter as a beautifully readable cutaway. One young bean sprout, only a small hook-like pale green shoot curling above the soil surface. Below soil, one attached bean and a long white main root growing DOWN with several fine side roots. Make correct simple continuous anatomy: seed to short shoot up, seed to long branching root down. NO fully opened leaves yet. Place two vivid but restrained orange handwritten field notes with slim clear arrows: "shoot up" pointing toward the shoot above soil; "root down" pointing downward beside the main root below soil. Arrow down is straight simple and pedagogical, no magical root eyes. Root responds to gravity; no root faces, hands or thinking. Pair very small at left looking together toward this mechanism, with Little leaning a little closer and Big quietly beside. Soft window light, faint garden, minimal potting cloth on windowsill; full scenic illustration with breathing paper margins. Labels only, no title, paragraph, footer, logo, numbers, grid, collage, worksheet, photo look or toy texture. The bean root is the hero, paired guides remain quiet flat diagram actors.

Match its illustrated flat gouache, pencil outlines, soft cream paper and sage windowsill, minimal flat pebble parent-child pair and pale clay pot. No photographic texture, no realism or 3D. New question served (NOT written): "What can a leaf do that a seed cannot?" One coherent botanical scene on the same sunlit windowsill later in growth. The bean plant now stands on one slender stem above the pot with two beautiful open green simple bean leaves and a little new bud. Main hero is leaves in a softly painted pale golden shaft of daylight. The clay pot is shown in cutaway with a correctly attached branching root reaching through soil. Integrate THREE small, clear orange handwritten notes around the actual plant: "light" with a thin ray arrow from window TO leaf, "air" with a little arrow from surrounding air INTO leaf, "water" with a fine arrow UP beside stem from roots TOWARD leaf. These inputs meet at the leaves; no sugars illustrated as fruit or snacks. Plant is centered/right, the pair small at lower left sharing attention to the leaves, Big 1.5x Little height, steady and slightly behind. Round warm-grey paper-wash pebble silhouettes with tiny dot eyes, tiny integrated ear nubs and no clothes, fur, hands or toy features. Soft garden silhouettes beyond window, spare cloth at pot base; full single scene with comfortable cream edge, botanical beauty, calm caring luxury. No numbers, title, footer, other words, poster, grid, collage, clipart, logos or neon. Diagram cues stay legible and science-centered.

Create ONE NEW landscape 3:2 single-scene Wonder Together Curiosity illustration, the quiet concluding companion in a botanical series. Attached image is STYLE AND CHARACTER reference only: same hand-painted flat gouache, delicate pencil ink, cream paper, sage window, pale clay pot, simple warm-grey Pebble Guides. No photograph or 3D. Question served (NOT printed): "How could we notice a change too slow to watch?" ONE coherent scene at the same windowsill: leafy bean plant with two open leaves and a new bud in an intact pale clay pot, afternoon garden light. A plain slender wooden measuring stick stands next to stem, its BOTTOM AT SOIL LEVEL, with a few dark marks but NO numbers. Beside it one small tied paper marker lower on stick records yesterday's height. Put two restrained orange handwritten labels with delicate leader lines: "earlier" pointing precisely to that lower tied mark and "today" pointing to the upper tip of the bean plant, which is higher than the mark. These are comparison cues, no exact measurements printed. In foreground an open notebook with ONLY two simple pencil plant sketches at different heights, NO WORDS OR NUMBERS, lying naturally on windowsill, and one plain pencil. Notebook is incidental to ONE scenic moment, not inset panels. Pebble pair small left, together looking from notebook to plant, Big 1.5x Little height beside and slightly behind. Flat rounded capsule silhouettes, tiny dot eyes and subtle nose dash, tiny ear nubs, no fingers, fur, clothes, toys, snouts or mascot anatomy. Scientific honesty: same baseline, plant height measured above soil; illustration not a scale ruler. No extra plants crowding scene. Warm calm full-scene storytelling, exquisite restraint, paper breathing around shapes, caring luxury. No poster, title, footer, logo, worksheet, collage, split scene, photorealistic texture, sparkles, neon or decorative saturated color.
